newsitem.title: USA: Factory Card supplier plans cutbacks.
newsitem.headline: Factory Card supplier plans cutbacks.

text.p: Factory Card Outlet Corp said Tuesday it was notified that Party Express, the party goods division of Hallmark Cards Inc, will stop shipping some party goods to it as of November 30.
The goods affected include many Walt Disney Co Warner Bros licensed products.

"The company believes that this decision will not have a material impact on its earnings for its fiscal year ending June 27, 1998, but could impact earnings beyond that date," Charles Cumello, president, said in a statement.
He said the company is continuing discussions with Hallmark, Disney and Warner Bros to attempt to resolve this situation or allow it to acquire the licensed product through other sources.
No reason was given for Party Goods' decision to stop shipping the products.
The company was not immediately available for comment.
Factory Card outlet is a chain of superstores that sell party supplies, greeting cards and special occasion merchandise.

"We look forward to the coming year as we continue our rapid superstore growth and expect to increase sales and profits to record levels," Cumello said. "The company plans to open approximately 50 new superstores, of which 49 leases have already been signed."

He said Factory Card expects about 35 to 40 superstores to be opened by Christmas 1997, of which 12 have opened so far. It opened 35 new superstores in fiscal 1997, ended June 28. As of August 19, it operated 149 stores in 19 states.
Earlier, Factory Card reported earnings for the fourth quarter of $2.3 million or $0.29 a share on 8.0 million shares outstanding.
That compares with $1.5 million or $0.30 a share on 5.0 million shares outstanding a year ago.
For fiscal 1997, it earned $1.7 million or $0.26 a share on 6.6 million shares outstanding, after a $312,886 or $0.05 a share debt retirement charge.
